canonical_topic: Capacity factor by solar tracking technology
definition: Different solar panel mounting technologies (fixed, single-axis tracking, dual-axis tracking) achieve different ranges of capacity factor by more closely following the sun's position.
core_idea: Adding tracking motion to solar panels increases efficiency and capacity factor relative to a fixed panel, with dual-axis tracking outperforming single-axis, which in turn outperforms fixed installations.
key_points: One-axis (east-west) tracking: 25-30% more efficient than fixed panels, with 17-25% capacity factor.
Two-axis tracking (east-west plus tilt): 30-40% more efficient than fixed panels, with 18-27.5% capacity factor.
Efficiency gains from tracking come from keeping panels more directly oriented toward the sun as it moves through the sky.
relationships: Directly extends the general solar capacity factor range described alongside it.
trading_implications: Knowing which tracking technology underlies a given solar asset helps refine generation forecasts and valuation versus using a single blended capacity-factor assumption.
caveats: The percentage efficiency gains (25-30%, 30-40%) describe relative improvement in output versus a fixed panel, not the absolute capacity factor itself.
